Subject: Level-to-local salary index reconciliation for APAC hub launches

Team —

Following up on last quarter's ask to produce a defensible offer anchoring method for our new APAC hubs (Jakarta, Manila). Attached are the draft market benchmarks and a proposed level_translation_matrix.xlsx that maps Redwood bands (L3-L7) to local pay slabs using market median + skill premium percentiles.

What I need from you this week:
- Karthik: quick pass on whether the translation multiplier (column D) should be additive vs multiplicative for senior ICs in Jakarta. We saw outliers in the recruiter feedback.
- Laura: confirmation on whether we keep the current manager uplift rule (+12% above IC median) or collapse to a flat band for small markets.
- Neha: any regulatory or payroll constraints we should bake into the matrix (local benefits, contractor conversion guardrails).

Notes: Mercer sample was used for core medians; vendor notes attached. I highlighted 3 roles with supply scarcity where I propose using the 75th percentile as the offer anchor. If we agree, I'll ask Finance and Recruiting to bake this into offer templates and the headcount approval checklist.

Attachments: APAC_market_benchmarks_Q3.pdf, level_translation_matrix.xlsx

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Hiring Strategy | Redwood Inference

Thanks for pulling this together, Tessa — good work. Quick notes from my side after skimming the matrix and recruiter conversations: 

- For senior ICs (L5-L7) in Jakarta I recommend a multiplicative multiplier (x1.07–x1.12) rather than an additive uplift. The market shows percentage compression rather than fixed-dollar gaps.
- For Manila, where currency volatility is high, anchor to local median but set a hard cap in USD equivalent to avoid offer swings when converting.
- Scarcity skills (ML infra, inference runtime) should get a role-level premium; I'd prefer tagging those roles in the matrix (column: skill_premium_flag).

Also flagged a potential legal/payroll snag: contractor conversions in Indonesia require a minimum local benefits contribution that effectively raises total comp by ~6–8%. Neha, can you confirm and add to the payroll checklist?

If we adopt multiplicative approach, I can update the sheet and re-run offer scenarios for FY27 hiring bands.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Tessa / Karthik —

Thanks for sending the matrix. A few clarifying points on methodology attached (mercers_methodology_notes.docx):
- Our median figures are computed on base pay only; we recommend using total cash adjustments where local benefits are material.
- The multiplicative approach is appropriate where the underlying currency distributions are log-normal (Jakarta fits this). For thin markets (Manila, some PH subsamples), we advise blending median with a small sample smoothing (we used n-bootstrapping).
- For scarcity roles, Mercer suggests benchmarking to the 60th–75th percentile depending on retention risk; they supplied a scarcity index which we've included in the doc.

We can provide a short addendum with sample offer bands if you want — Ami from our APAC practice (cc'd on separate thread) can run a 2-market simulation.

Regards,
Mercer Compensation Analytics
benchmarks@mercer.com

Thanks — this thread is exactly the level of detail I want before we roll new anchors. Decision items: 

1) Approve multiplicative multiplier for senior ICs in Jakarta per Karthik's recommendation. Please update the sheet and produce a red/amber/green offer sensitivity table (sensitivity = impact on FY27 comp budget) by EOD Wednesday.
2) For Manila, set anchor = local median with an USD equivalent cap (Finance to define cap; I've looped them into HROPS-712).
3) Scarcity roles: accept benchmarking to 60th–75th percentile. Karthik, flag roles and I will sign off on the final list.
4) Neha: confirm contractor conversion cost and add to the offer approval checklist; if >7% uplift then require a headcount re-evaluation step.

Once the updated matrix and the sensitivity table are in Drive, recruiting will be authorized to use the new anchors for any offers issued after 2026-12-01. Tessa, please coordinate with Finance and Recruiting for the rollout comms.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations | Redwood Inference
